annotation_description: Cast Quantum Riddler via Warp before playing the Botanical Sanctum from hand. Playing the land first would provide an additional untapped mana source, which could be relevant for responding to opponent's plays or casting whatever card is drawn from Riddler's ETB trigger.

With exactly 3 lands (Hallowed Fountain, Abandoned Air Temple, Floodfarm Verge) that can produce 1WW, casting Ajani, Outland Chaperone would be a stronger turn 3 play than Floodpits Drowner. Ajani is a planeswalker that generates incremental value through token creation and can threaten removal of tapped creatures. The Drowner's flash means it could be cast on the opponent's turn later, and its ETB tap ability is best used reactively. Playing Ajani first maximizes the value of having priority on turn 3 while the opponent has limited board presence (just a 1/2 Gene Pollinator and lands).

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Ajani, Outland Chaperone
chosen_display: 1. +1: Create a 1/1 green and white Kithkin creature token.
annotation_description: The opponent has Badgermole Cub (2/2) and Keen-Eyed Curator (3/3) on the battlefield. Gene Pollinator and all lands are tapped, so there are no tapped creatures to target with the -2. However, looking more carefully at the board state, the opponent's Gene Pollinator IS tapped. Ajani's -2 deals 4 damage to target tapped creature - Gene Pollinator is tapped and could be killed. While Gene Pollinator is likely a smaller threat than the Keen-Eyed Curator or Badgermole Cub, killing it for free with Ajani's -2 removes a creature and is better than making a 1/1 token when facing down 3/3 and 2/2 creatures. The +1 creating a 1/1 chump blocker has some value, but removing an opponent's creature (even a small one) is generally more impactful, especially since Ajani is at 3 loyalty and going to 4 with +1 gives survivability. This is debatable - the +1 protects Ajani and builds board presence, but using -2 on Gene Pollinator removes a creature that generates value (pollinating/token making). Actually, Gene Pollinator is a 1/1 that likely has useful abilities. Killing it with a -2 (going to 1 loyalty) seems risky as Ajani becomes very vulnerable. The +1 to go to 4 loyalty while making a blocker is reasonable defensive play. On reflection, this is close to reasonable given Ajani's loyalty concerns.

By not sending Gene Pollinator (1/2) to attack alongside Keen-Eyed Curator and Badgermole Cub, Ajani survives at 1 loyalty instead of dying. With all opponent lands tapped, there was no combat trick risk. Ajani at 1 loyalty can still use its -2 next turn to deal 4 damage to a tapped creature, removing one of Opus Analyst's threats.

With only 4 mana available (4 untapped lands, Gene Pollinator can convert one to any color but doesn't add net mana), Quantum Riddler's full cost of {3}{U}{U} (5 mana) appears uncastable. If they somehow cast it via Warp for {1}{U}, they'd lose it at end step again. Better to use Keen-Eyed Curator's ability to exile Floodpits Drowner from opponent's graveyard (working toward the 4-card-type bonus) or save mana.

Casting Aven Interrupter during precombat main phase is suboptimal. It has flash, so it could be held to cast on the opponent's turn to exile a spell they cast. Additionally, casting it now before combat means the opponent sees the 2/2 flyer before blocks are relevant, and more importantly, the Aven's ETB ability to exile a spell requires a spell on the stack - there's no spell to exile right now, wasting the ETB trigger. Furthermore, Voice of Victory (which prevents opponents from casting spells during your turn) could have been cast first, then Aven Interrupter could be saved for the opponent's turn to get value from its ETB exile ability.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Gene Pollinator (1/2) was sent at the player for 1 damage instead of at Ajani (3 loyalty). Ajani is actively generating value with +1 tokens each turn and threatens -2 removal on tapped creatures. Reducing Ajani's loyalty is generally worth more than 1 point of player damage. Additionally, attacking with Gene Pollinator at all is questionable since it's a mana dork that could be kept back for mana production.

Opus Analyst has 2 untapped lands (Botanical Sanctum and Forest) and a Quantum Riddler in hand costing {3}{U}{U}, which can't be cast for full cost. However, Quantum Riddler has Warp {1}{U}, which costs exactly 2 mana and could be cast with the untapped Botanical Sanctum + Forest. This would give a 4/6 flyer that draws a card on entry, even though it exiles at end step. That's a free cantrip plus potential pressure, pure value that was left on the table. Nature's Rhythm for X=0 would find nothing useful, so passing on that is fine, but the Quantum Riddler Warp cast was missed.

Cast High Noon apparently believing it could remove a creature, but its sacrifice ability costs {4}{R} and KimiK2 has no red mana sources. The 'one spell per turn' restriction also hurts KimiK2's own ability to deploy their hand (Voice of Victory, Floodpits Drowner). The reasoning explicitly states wanting to 'eliminate one of their biggest threats' which High Noon cannot do here.

With High Noon on the stack (which will prevent casting more than one spell per turn), KimiK2 has a window to flash in Floodpits Drowner before the restriction takes effect. The Drowner would tap Quantum Riddler (4/6 flyer) and put a stun counter on it, neutralizing the biggest threat. After High Noon resolves, they cannot cast another spell this turn, so this is the last chance to deploy the Drowner.

Declined to activate Agna Qel'a's loot ability ({2}{U}, {T}: draw a card, discard a card) despite having plenty of untapped lands to both activate it AND keep mana open for Floodpits Drowner ({1}{U} flash) on opponent's turn. Since High Noon was already cast this turn (and it limits to one spell per turn), the mana had no other spell-casting use this turn. Looting is pure card quality improvement at no real cost.

KimiK2 Diplom passed without activating Agna Qel'a's loot ability ({2}{U}, {T}: Draw a card, then discard a card) and ended up not casting any spells this turn either, completely wasting their mana. With High Noon restricting each player to one spell per turn, using mana sinks when not casting spells is important for maintaining card quality, especially when behind on board.

message: Select a creature an opponent controls
annotation_description: KimiK2 used Ajani's -2 (4 damage to a tapped creature) on Badgermole Cub (2/2) instead of the more threatening Keen-Eyed Curator (3/3 base, potentially 7/7 with trample). The Curator is a much bigger threat that could take over the game if it reaches 4+ card types exiled. Quantum Riddler (4/6) survives 4 damage so it's not a valid kill target, making Curator the clear best choice.

At 2 HP facing lethal next turn from opponent's board, KimiK2 Diplom declined to activate Agna Qel'a's loot ability ({2}{U}, {T}: draw then discard), which is a free card quality improvement that could dig for survival tools. The reasoning was completely disconnected from the actual board state, referencing Voice of Victory which isn't on the battlefield.
